🇲🇽🌎 <u>WHAT THE EU TRADE DEAL ACTUALLY COSTS — UAM ECONOMIST WARNS DIVERSIFICATION ≠ SOVEREIGNTY</u>

"Toda apertura comercial sin protección política es sinónimo de subordinación," writes UAM Iztapalapa economist Carolina Hernández Calvario in Contralínea, breaking down the May 22 Mexico-EU modernized trade deal: $94.5B bilateral trade in 2025, 35% growth projected over five years — and European firms now compete equally for Mexican public procurement, locking in foreign access to energy and critical minerals. Trading US dependency for European dependency is not sovereignty, she warns. Industrial policy is. Domestic suppliers are. State enterprises are.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM TAKES THE STAGE AT MONUMENTO A LA REVOLUCIÓN TODAY — 32-STATE ACCOUNTABILITY EVENT</u>

At 11 AM today, two years after her electoral landslide, Claudia Sheinbaum convenes Mexicans at the Monumento a la Revolución for a public accounting of her first 18 months — broadcast simultaneously across plazas in 31 states (Coahuila excluded for local elections). "En México, los mexicanos deciden — nadie más," she has framed the event, a direct response to the months-long foreign-interference push from Washington and the domestic opposition. "No robamos, no mentimos, y nunca los vamos a traicionar." The Zócalo is being held back for World Cup Fan Fest setup.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>AICM PHASE 1 DELIVERED — 6.5B PESOS, PAID BY THE AIRPORT ITSELF, NOT TAXPAYERS</u>

"Misión cumplida," Sheinbaum declared as the Navy handed over the first phase of Mexico City's airport renovation 11 days before the World Cup opens. The 6.5 billion pesos came from AICM's own operating profits — not the public budget — a deliberate break from the privatized-concession model. Capacity now reaches 46 operations per hour, with new fast-exit taxiways D1 and D2, an anti-drone system, and free Wi-Fi. Phases 2 and 3 follow toward a 10 billion peso total. The Navy built it. The airport paid for it.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>CUBA READIES FOR WAR — ISLAND BRACES AS US STACKS NIMITZ + SPY FLIGHTS IN CARIBBEAN</u>

"Cuba does not desire war, but is prepared to defend itself," Parlatino president Rolando González Patricio told La Jornada from Mexico City, calling this the island's most critical moment since the Bay of Pigs. The USS Nimitz carrier group has parked in the Caribbean since May 21 — alongside intensified spy flights and a "genocidal" financial-energy blockade — and Cuba's "war of all the people" doctrine is already operational. Mexico remains the only nation that has opposed the US embargo since the 1960s.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>MOODY'S: PEMEX WILL NEED GOVERNMENT SUPPORT THROUGH 2028 — MEXICO PAID $40B IN 2025, BUDGETED $14B FOR 2026</u>

Moody's warned this week that Pemex will require federal financial support through at least 2028, missing the Strategic Plan 2025-2035 target of weaning off public support by 2027. The agency cited negative free cash flow through 2028, depleted mature fields, and elevated debt maturities — and estimates Pemex will need an average $11 billion in annual investment from 2026 to 2028.

The Mexican government backed Pemex with over $40 billion in 2025 and budgeted another $14 billion for 2026, most of it covering short-term debt service.

Wall Street calls this "structural pressure." We call it national strategy: Mexico funding its own oil company instead of selling it off to BlackRock and Halliburton like the neoliberals did with everything else. Pemex stays public. The state stays sovereign.

🇲🇽 <u>CHAMBER APPROVES INTEGRITY COMMISSION TO VET CANDIDATES — 271-92 VOTE BLOCKS NARCO MONEY FROM ELECTORAL POLITICS</u>

The Chamber of Deputies approved 271-92 the creation of an integrity verification commission to screen candidates and aspiring public officials for links to illicit activities. The body will consist of three INE counselors, with the National Electoral Institute setting operating protocols and data management rules.

The vote came amid the broader 16-hour Senate sprint that also passed foreign-interference nullification clauses (307-128) and postponed the 2027 judicial election to 2028. Together the reforms close two doors at once: narco money in candidacies, and foreign meddling in elections.

This is what a sovereign democracy hardening itself against US embassy interference looks like — written into law, with numbers on the board.

🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM FROM ALMOLOYA: "WE WILL NOT RETURN TO THE REGIME OF CORRUPTION AND PRIVILEGE"</u>

President Sheinbaum responded to the escalating interference campaign directly from Almoloya, Estado de México: "the people are strong, empowered, and the conquests of the people are defended." She rejected the "dirty campaigns on social networks and media" pushed by conservatives "allied with foreign interests" trying to restore the old regime.

"We will not return to the regime of corruption and privileges," she declared, calling on organized citizens to defend the social welfare gains of the 4T. She characterized the entire interference operation as destined to fail because "the people are organized and there is democracy."

Tomorrow's nationwide accountability event in all 32 plazas — celebrating 2 years of the second floor of the 4T — is the popular answer to the conspiracy.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>CONTRALÍNEA EXPOSÉ: US AMBASSADOR JOHNSON, CIA, DEA & MEXICAN RIGHT COORDINATING TO BREAK SHEINBAUM BEFORE 2027</u>

Contralínea's weekly investigation maps a coordinated operation against Mexico: meetings between US embassy officials and PAN/PRI/MC/PVEM leaders, CIA activity in opposition-governed border states (Chihuahua under Maru Campos at the center), media-driven "narco-government" propaganda, and a push for capital flight and tax non-compliance to manufacture an artificial economic crisis.

Sheinbaum herself confirmed the pattern: "there's a link between international organizations or organizations of other countries and the Mexican right" — and reminded everyone that "in Mexico the people decide, no one else decides more than the people. There are no external voters."

Trump already telegraphed the threat: his government "began the land phase" of drug operations and warned "if authorities aren't going to do the job, we will." That's not policy. That's an ultimatum.

🚨🇨🇺 <u>SOUTHCOM CHIEF MEETS CUBAN GENERALS AT GUANTÁNAMO — FIRST SUCH MEETING IN RECENT MEMORY</u>

US Southern Command head Gen. Francis Donovan met with Cuban military commanders at the perimeter of the Guantánamo naval base — the first such SOUTHCOM-Cuba meeting in recent memory, confirmed today by both governments. The Cuban delegation was led by Gen. Roberto Legra Sotolongo, first vice minister of the General Staff.

The meeting follows CIA Director John Ratcliffe's unprecedented Havana visit earlier in May, and comes as Cuba publishes civil defense guides for the public against potential US military aggression. 30+ US legislators already wrote Trump demanding he abandon any war plans against the island.

When SOUTHCOM and the CIA both show up at your perimeter in the same month, it's not diplomacy. It's pre-attack reconnaissance.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>UNESCO: US ENERGY BLOCKADE PUTS CUBAN EDUCATION AT RISK — TEACHERS, SCHOOL YEAR CUT</u>

UNESCO's regional office in Havana confirmed today that the US energy embargo against Cuba is endangering education across the island. Fuel and transport shortages keep teachers from reaching classrooms, deepening a national deficit of over 26,000 educators.

Cuba's government was forced to shorten school hours and end the academic year weeks early — a calendar normally running through late June, cut short by Trump's January sanctions threatening any country that sells crude to Havana. UNESCO warned the situation "endangers the future of an entire generation, with long-term consequences."

This is what the blockade looks like in 2026: kids robbed of class so Washington can starve an island into submission.
